checksDetailed.detail: The fixed-source Host Emulated workflow explicitly checks out head 86f52244. Both complete logs show Node v24.21.0, Linux x64, the original eight-file unfiltered Node command, one installer-helper command, one selected Xvfb GUI invocation and the unchanged whole post-flow verifier. Team alone also runs the original ten-file serialized Runtime/Team command and workspace typechecks/lint. Both 52,410-byte printed verifier scripts match the source run block byte-for-byte after YAML indentation removal. No retry/filter substitution is present in the selected GUI invocations.

Each original common command reports 247/247 passing, zero failures/cancellations/skips/todos. Its exact ordered 247 titles match across both jobs. The Team UI file contributes all 149 consecutive titles, preserving the original 164,965-byte/139-case prefix and adding only the accepted awaited ten-case import. Team's separate ten-file command reports 184/184 passing; the installer helper reports 7/7 in each job. These are per-command/per-job outcomes, not a sum of unique coverage or GUI case counts. Direct test declarations are not registration counts: backend-observations has 39 direct declarations but 63 reported cases; settings and catalog also expand parameterized cases.

The selected private fixture environment is constructed from explicit TEST paths, not inherited user credentials. Startup orchestrator/Claude/Codex/OpenCode paths point to private finite sentinels; the only retained sentinel invocation in either job is the allowed finite claude-multimodel --version. Selection's exact runtime and management executables are the pinned TEST-codex-peer wrapper; it verifies source realpaths and full hashes before importing finite providerPeer/providerDesktopPeer. The selected branch admits only declared private paths, roles, argv and TEST markers. No evidence here qualifies or authorizes a real Claude/Codex binary, version, account or model.

The frozen generic runtime UI entry returns early to the original Selection driver for this selected mode. The installer branch is not selected. The provider/SDK/production parser is not replaced by this outcome audit. Runtime peer behavior is finite Node protocol behavior with local Host MCP, not an actual vendor process.

The original controls require owned renderer checks, unique visible target lookup, positive geometry, center hit and not-disabled state, stable target samples, a final exact point reread and currentness before one physical press/release. Uncertain clicks are not replayed. The ordinary Create form uses original navigation and Input events, not direct business API mutation. Passive input records are evidence only and do not confer authority.

The Team driver reads the seed's canonical Task, reaches the original sidebar/Open team/Task dialog/Subject/Create controls, issues one original Create click, and requires exactly one matching completed TEST-human task.create command. The archived before/after task arrays show one unchanged seed plus the exact new Task. The original reload changes performance.timeOrigin and the driver then deep-compares the full reloaded canonical Task array with the original after array. The proof retains a final same-ID/product-fields assertion. This is offline Task persistence, not Runtime readiness or Team launch.

Team A launches once as TEST-model/low. Team B is created through the original save-only form as Codex/TEST-model-next/high; the original owner read must have no runtime captures before launch. One published TEST-human creation record and savedSelection join. After a real renderer reload the original driver compares the entire B owner with its pre-reload bSaved value, hydrates the saved controls and launches B once; the captured definition and actual finite Runtime thread both carry TEST-model-next/high. The archive retains the receipt/captured definition, not a separately archived full B owner file; equality is supported by the executed source assertion and passing original flow.

Five original observation checkpoints retain A's full binding, configuration, Host incarnation, session reference and exact finite thread; nativeReady is true. The first four also require unchanged original inputs. During B Stop, the fifth intentionally records originalInputsUnchanged=false because A has its new pending stream; the source separately deep-compares that exact pending input before/after B Stop. It would be incorrect to call the false field a failure or claim all inputs were unchanged throughout.

The original A message.send has one command/input identity and exactly one TEST_UI_STREAM effect. A partial response appears while input is nonterminal. B's one scoped Stop reaches closed/released plus original PID absence without changing A. The fixture writes only its exclusive TEST release-stream gate once, then the original A input reaches succeeded and the UI displays completion. A is then stopped once with the same closed/released/absence requirements. No business mutation retry or replacement input is used.

Each flow requests ordinary Quit, observes its original app ChildProcess exit 0/no signal and begins cleanup with one captured-group orphan esbuild row. The unchanged natural-exit observer, under the remaining original 3,000 ms observation interval, requires the exact original app exit, no leader reappearance, fresh whole-group absence, captured Host absence and all originally captured descendants absent. Both receipts take that settled natural-drain path, with no group signal escalation. Selection separately observes all 50 original peer PIDs absent. This is retained TEST-scope cleanup, not global process absence.
